text:
alex: monitoring-bot just fired a GPU_ECC_ERROR alert for cluster-us-west-2. host=gpu-node-41 gpu_id=3. seeing a spike in Xid/ECC logs :frowning:

monitoring-bot: Alert GPU_ECC_ERROR firing (severity=page). labels={cluster=us-west-2, instance=gpu-node-41, gpu_id=3}. value=5 events in last 5m.

maria: ack. is this a single host flapping or a fleet signal?

sam: looks noisy. dcgm_exporter metrics show small spikes from gpu-node-41 and gpu-node-42 every ~10-20m. counts reset after driver restart. suspect flaky card + driver churn.

jen: thanks. can we tune Prometheus rules so we don't page on single short blips? that cluster is noisy during nightly batch jobs and we're drowning in alerts.

alex: yeah we should avoid page for 1-off Xid errors. propose two changes: 1) use increase() over a longer window, 2) require sustained rate or multiple GPUs on the same host.

sam: +1. concrete suggestion: change alert to use increase over 1h and require >3 uncorrectable ECC events, and only become P1 if >5 events across any 3 GPUs on a host.

maria: can you paste a draft PromQL?

sam: sure:

```yaml
alert: GPU_ECC_NOISY
expr: increase(dcgm_ecc_uncorrectable_total{job="dcgm-exporter"}[1h]) > 3
for: 30m
labels: {severity="warning"}
annotations: {summary="Noisy ECC on {{ $labels.instance }} GPU {{ $labels.gpu_id }}"}
```

sam: and for escalation to page:

```promql
sum by (instance) (increase(dcgm_ecc_uncorrectable_total{job="dcgm-exporter"}[1h])) > 5
```

jen: I like that. Also add max_over_time(increase(...)[6h]) to catch long-tail degradation?

alex: maybe instead of raw count we use rate + cardinality: e.g., count of GPUs with increase(...) > 0 over 1h. if count >= 3 then page. avoids single-gpu flaps.

maria: good call. example:

```promql
count by (instance) ( (increase(dcgm_ecc_uncorrectable_total{job="dcgm-exporter"}[1h]) > 0) ) >= 3
```

ops-bot: Note: there is an existing runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/GPUECC-Runbook — includes drain/replace play, driver restart steps, and tagging flaky nodes.

jen: we should also add an exclusion list for nodes already marked 'replace_pending' label to avoid repeated alerts during hardware replacement.

sam: agree — add `instance!~"label=replace_pending"` or use node labels from kubernetes service discovery.

alex: operationally, if rule change reduces noise we still need a semi-automated triage:
- low severity (warning): aggregated >0 but <3 GPUs => create ticket, tag node, schedule diagnostics.
- high severity (page): >=3 GPUs or host-sum >5 => run drain-and-replace runbook and open incident.

maria: what's the capacity impact if we start draining hosts? cluster-us-west-2 has 120 GPUs, losing 2 nodes (~16 GPUs) might bump the autoscaler. we should include cost/throughput note in the runbook.

jen: I can add a short blurb to the runbook about capacity thresholds and when to contact capacity team.

sam: I pushed a branch with the proto rule to prometheus-alerts repo: https://git.internal/redwood/alerts/pull/234. please review.

alex: tagging @oncall for review later today so we can roll config at 2pm UTC if no objections.

maria: Quick question — do we also tune DCGM exporter scrape intervals? if exporter scrapes every 15s noise could be more visible. maybe move to 30s for noisy nodes.

sam:I don't love per-node scrape changes. prefer smoothing in alerts rather than changing scrape cadence. but we could add a scrape relabel to drop some metrics for nodes known noisy.

jen: let's do alert-side smoothing first. if noise persists we'll consider export-side changes.

ops-bot: deployment scheduled: prometheus-alerts#234 -> staging at 14:00 UTC. rollback window 30m.

alex: great. after staging let's watch firehose for 2 hours. if alerts drop to baseline we ship to prod. if not we revert and revisit. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks everyone — this should cut down on noisy wakeups and make real regressions stand out.

jen: I'll update the runbook and add the capacity note.

sam: leaving a note in the PR about tests and alert history graphs. link the grafana panel for ECC trends.

alex: closing this thread after prod deploy. follow-up in #incidents if anything pages.
